newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten says Hong Kong budget right for transition.
newsitem.headline: Patten says Hong Kong budget right for transition.

text.p: Hong Kong governor Chris Patten said on Wednesday the government's budget for the fiscal year starting April 1 hit the right note for the territory's transition to Chinese sovereignty on June 30.
"(Financial Secretary) Donald Tsang has struck the right note for the transition," Patten said in a statement.
"He has stuck faithfully but creatively to the financial policies which are at the heart of Hong Kong's spectacular success, and which provide the foundations for its future growth," he said.
Patten noted Hong Kong was able to cut taxes, boost spending on social services and infrastructure and bolster reserves for the fifth year in a row.

He added the community should especially appreciate the focus on tax concessions for the middle, or "sandwich", class and the continuing commitment to improving services to the disadvantaged and deserving.
